A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CoDD, with the same authors and core research framework. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CoDD experiments with LLaDA and Dream, computational-cost measurements, hyperparameter ablations, and qualitative generation examples.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds WikiText generation and conditional-likelihood evaluations in Section 7.

M1.justification: Section 5.2 and Algorithm 2 replace multiple windows covering all target tokens with one fixed-size window covering the most targets. The revised algorithm additionally requires more than one target within the window before activating PC guidance and changes the state-update rule to sample within that window while preserving positions outside it. The core architecture, training objective, and block-diffusion procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds WikiText-103 validation experiments for open-ended continuation and ground-truth completion likelihood, extending evaluation beyond the retained reasoning and coding benchmarks. It also introduces GPT-2-generated text as PC training data for these experiments, substantially broadening the represented language data and task requirements.

E2.justification: The new Figure 4 evaluates SEDD and SEDD augmented with Discrete Copula Diffusion against CoDD. These were discussed or cited but not evaluated as comparators in v1. This is a localized comparator expansion; the existing reasoning, decoding-heuristic, and reinforcement-learning comparison sets are retained.

E3.justification: Section 7 adds distinct evaluation protocols: randomly truncated prefixes, Dream continuation at 16/32/64 steps measured using perplexity, diversity, repetition, and NLL per token, and SEDD completion likelihood averaged within context-length buckets. These substantially extend the evaluation design beyond the retained accuracy and latency protocols. Appendix B's correction from Dream 8B to 7B matches the model already specified in both main texts.

E4.justification: The new WikiText likelihood curves examine whether comparative gains persist across context lengths, adding a focused sensitivity analysis. The mask-ratio analysis, activation-threshold and temperature ablations, and two qualitative reasoning examples remain. The first appendix ablation is relabeled from MATH500 to GPQA without changing its numerical entries.

E5.justification: The existing likelihood boxplots are retained. The added experiments report point estimates and bucket means without introducing repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or another uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds WikiText results: Dream-to-CoDD perplexity changes from 3.32 to 2.92, 4.67 to 4.08, and 4.66 to 4.15 at 16/32/64 steps, accompanied by lower diversity and higher repetition. Figure 4 adds likelihood results favoring CoDD over DCD and unaugmented SEDD across context buckets. Existing reasoning and appendix scores remain numerically unchanged; these additions are new experimental results, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Equation (5) changes the stated PC factor from p_omega(x0) to p_omega(x0 | xt), explicitly adding conditioning to the joint-distribution definition. This is a localized mathematical edit: the other definitions, objective, theorem, and derivations remain. Appendix D still uses the unconditional factor, leaving the reconciliation unexplained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about addressing factorization with tractable PC guidance, inexpensive training, and improved few-step generation. The new natural-language experiments supply additional support without redefining these main contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of the WikiText results, attributing increased repetition to concentration in higher-density language regions and treating near-baseline diversity as evidence against collapse. It also interprets likelihood gains as recovery of inter-token dependencies. The existing high-mask-ratio limitation and proposed dynamic structural remedies are retained.

D1.justification: v3 discloses GPT-2-generated samples as the PC training source for the new natural-language experiments and corrects Appendix B's Dream model designation to 7B. Existing optimizer, hardware, generation-length, sampling-parameter, and code-access disclosures remain. The new experiments do not specify the reference language model or sample counts.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning beyond the earlier diffusion-focused discussion with a dedicated account of PC/HMM language modeling and controlled generation. It explicitly distinguishes CoDD from Conditional Sum-Product Networks and Probabilistic Neural Circuits that condition internal circuit parameters, and adds relevant diffusion and correlation-modeling work. The updated Liu image-inpainting reference is the same previously cited work, not a new contribution.

P1.justification: v3 separates reasoning benchmarks from a new natural-language experiments section, shifts subsequent section numbering, adds acknowledgements, and updates publication information. Local grammar and typographical corrections accompany these changes, while most existing prose and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the WikiText metrics table and context-length likelihood plot, with corresponding page reflow and renumbering of later tables and figures. It corrects the first appendix ablation caption to GPQA. Existing plots, benchmark-table designs, and qualitative-example displays are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: Section 7 extends empirical support to ordinary-text generation and directly compares against DCD, while the expanded related work and appendix corrections improve positioning and clarity. These provide a modest net benefit. The new evaluation remains incompletely specified, lower perplexity accompanies greater repetition and reduced diversity, and Equation (5)'s conditioning edit is not reconciled with Appendix D. These limitations constrain the strength of the improvement.
